text.p: German steel makers Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp and Thyssen AG said in a joint statement on Wednesday they were holding talks on possible cooperation that could make the Krupp bid for Thyssen shares irrelevant.

The talks, aimed at reaching a common business strategy for the steel sector, must lead to an agreement within eight days, or the two companies would return to their original positions, the statement said.
The statement by the companies followed a similar statement released by the state government of North Rhine-Westphalia after a meeting of the three parties.

"A future-oriented concept, which was repeatedly considered in the past and has already led to successful joint ventures in the steel business, could solve the difficulties that both companies have in the steel sector," the statement said.
"This could lead on a partnership basis to a steel enterprise that takes a leading position in international rankings," it said.
On Tuesday, Thyssen vowed to defend itself against a rare hostile takeover bid by its smaller rival Krupp.
